leader.name: Daniel Ek
leader.caveat: Includes shares owned by Tencent that he votes under a proxy; his own holding is smaller.

structure.note: One class of ordinary shares plus beneficiary certificates, which 'carry no economic rights and are issued to provide the holders of such certificates additional voting rights'; each carries one vote. Ten certificates were issued per ordinary share held of record by entities of the founders, 309,932,980 in total at December 31, 2025. The 20-F gives Daniel Ek 28.8% and Martin Lorentzon 40.5% of total voting power; no single holder is stated to have a majority.

geography.basis: Revenue by country (Premium revenue by where the membership originates; Ad-Supported revenue by where the advertising campaign is delivered)

notes: Fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (data.js fy 'Dec 2025'). Spotify reports under IFRS in euros, so values are billions of EUR (converted from € millions, no FX). Source is the FY2025 Form 20-F (accession 0001628280-26-006874); buybacks and stock comp match SEC XBRL. OWNERSHIP is as of December 31, 2025, from Item 7.A. LEADER: the 20-F lists Daniel Ek as 'Founder and Executive Chairman', with Alex Norström and Gustav Söderström as Co-Chief Executive Officers (Ek moved from CEO to Executive Chairman on January 1, 2026). PROXY SHARES: Ek's 28,625,267 ordinary shares (13.9%) are what the 20-F reports as his beneficial ownership. They include shares he only votes: footnote (1) says 11,993,298 are held by D.G.E. Investments, which he owns indirectly, and that he votes the shares held by TME Hong Kong, Image Frame, Tencent Mobility Limited and Distribution Pool Limited (all Tencent entities, 16,631,969 shares) through an irrevocable proxy held by D.G.E. Investments. 11,993,298 + 16,631,969 = 28,625,267, so the Tencent shares are inside his 13.9%. For reference only (computed, not stated in the filing): 11,993,298 / 205,832,527 is about 5.8%. TENCENT is listed in the 20-F at 16,631,969 ordinary shares, 8.1%. It is not added to largestHolders because those shares are already counted in Ek's figure (overlap rule). BENEFICIARY CERTIFICATES: Ek holds 119,932,980 (38.7%) and Lorentzon 190,000,000 (61.3%). They carry votes but no economic rights and are excluded from economic percentages. HOLDERS: Lorentzon's 9.3% includes 43,984 option shares exercisable within 60 days. Baillie Gifford, listed last year, no longer appears in the 5% table. DIVIDENDS: none ever paid. BUYBACKS: €439 million (US$510 million) for 768,223 shares under the repurchase program in 2025; the €241 million of employee taxes withheld on RSU releases is a separate line and excluded. STOCK COMP: the Note 5 personnel-expense line (€248 million, the XBRL-tagged figure); the cash-flow add-back is €247 million. PLAN: none described in the sections read.

ecosystem.notes: The 20-F states no total for royalties paid to rights holders (cost of revenue consists predominantly of royalty and distribution costs related to content streaming, but royalties are not broken out), so payouts is null. The study figure is Spotify's own from its Loud & Clear 2026 report, in US dollars (the filing reports in euros), stated as 'more than $11 billion', so 11 is a lower bound; it is money paid to the music industry as a whole (rights holders such as labels and publishers, not only artists). It is not audited filing data. It replaces the Loud & Clear 2025 figure ($10 billion for 2024). No volume measure exists, so measure is null.

footprint.notes: Two kinds of country data. (1) The FY2025 20-F itemises 2025 average employees only for the U.S. (3,466), Sweden (1,271) and the U.K. (887); it gives approximately 1,663 'employees and contractors' in aggregate across about 25 other countries, which is not a country row. (2) Loud & Clear 2026 (2025 data), from Spotify's own newsroom posts for that edition: Sweden (nearly SEK 2 billion, 'nära 2 miljarder kronor'), Brazil (approximately BRL 2 billion) and Canada (over CAD 544 million). No newer EU figure was found (checked Nov 24, 2026: the newsroom's Europe, European Union and Loud & Clear tags have no 2026 EU post), so the EU row keeps the Loud & Clear 2025 figure (€1.7 billion for 2024) and its metric keeps period 2024. Royalties are by artist origin, paid to rights holders, not to artists directly. Each currency is its own metric; they are not comparable or additive. Sweden has two rows because the employee and royalty figures come from different documents. India's 2026 post gives growth rates and thresholds but no total, so it is not recorded. Office lease space comes from Item 4.D (occupied space is lower: about 226,000 and 378,000 sq ft). The FY2025 20-F no longer lists a Minneapolis regional office, so that site was removed. No U.S. state data.

paidout.notes: Fiscal year ended December 31, 2025. IFRS filer, but it classifies interest paid (the only cash interest line; the financing section has no interest line) and income taxes in operating activities, so nothing is added back. Interest received (242) sits in operating cash flow; dividends received (23) are in investing. No intangible-purchase line; business combinations (9) excluded. FX: calendar-2025 average.

marketcap.notes: Spotify's ordinary shares are listed on the NYSE as SPOT (its only listing; not an ADR). No document states shares outstanding after September 30, 2026, so the count is computed from the Q3 2026 6-K (filed October 22, 2026): 210,741,268 issued minus 5,215,814 treasury shares. The FY2025 20-F cover gave 205,832,527 outstanding at December 31, 2025. Beneficiary certificates (309,932,980 at December 31, 2025) carry votes but no economic rights and are left out.

pay.notes: Employees: Spotify reports only an annual average of full-time employees (7,287 in 2025), not a year-end head count, so the average is used. Payroll: Note 5's total personnel expenses (€1,924 million: wages and salaries, social costs and payroll taxes, retirement contributions, €248 million of share-based compensation and other benefits), in billions of EUR. Social costs fell in 2025 largely because they include payroll taxes on share-based awards, which move with the share price.
